quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the flight was delayed by three hours, we still made our connecting train.
quests.completedSentence: Although the flight was delayed by three hours, we still made our connecting train.
quests.ruleExplanation: The long delay makes catching the connection surprising, and 'although' introduces that established fact despite which the outcome still happened.
quests.nativeTip: A three-hour delay should have ruined the connection, but somehow it didn't.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ she'd never coached before, the team improved dramatically under her.
quests.completedSentence: Although she'd never coached before, the team improved dramatically under her.
quests.ruleExplanation: Her lack of experience makes the team's progress unexpected, and 'although' sets up that fact the good outcome pushed past.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: The bakery kept its prices low, ___ ingredient costs kept rising each month.

quests.ruleExplanation: Keeping prices low despite rising costs is the surprising part, and 'although' introduces that fact working against the expected outcome.
quests.nativeTip: Rising costs would normally force prices up, yet the bakery held the line anyway.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: The instructions were confusing, ___ most guests eventually figured out the check-in kiosk.
quests.completedSentence: The instructions were confusing, though most guests eventually figured out the check-in kiosk.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ he'd studied the material carefully, the exam still caught him off guard.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession

quests.completedSentence: Even though the company posted record profits, it still laid off a quarter of its staff.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ she'd lived abroad for a decade, she never lost her hometown accent.
quests.completedSentence: Even though she'd lived abroad for a decade, she never lost her hometown accent.
quests.ruleExplanation: Ten years abroad makes the unchanged accent genuinely striking, and 'even though' emphasizes just how surprising that persistence is.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the bridge had just reopened, another crack appeared within weeks.
quests.completedSentence: Even though the bridge had just reopened, another crack appeared within weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: The recent reopening makes the new crack feel almost unbelievable, and 'even though' underlines that heightened sense of contradiction.
quests.nativeTip: A brand-new reopening makes a fresh crack especially alarming.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ unemployment dropped last quarter, wage growth remained flat.
quests.completedSentence: Although unemployment dropped last quarter, wage growth remained flat.
quests.ruleExplanation: The measured, statistical tone of a report fits the plainer, slightly formal 'although' better than the more casual or heavily emphatic alternatives.
quests.nativeTip: This reads like a neutral line from an economic report, not a casual chat.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: The soup was a bit too salty, ___ it was still pretty tasty.
quests.completedSentence: The soup was a bit too salty, though it was still pretty tasty.
quests.ruleExplanation: The relaxed wording and easy tone match casual speech, where 'though' is the natural, conversational choice.
quests.nativeTip: This sounds like something you'd say out loud to a friend, not write in a report.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ he'd broken his ankle just days before, he still ran the marathon.
quests.completedSentence: Even though he'd broken his ankle just days before, he still ran the marathon.
quests.ruleExplanation: A recently broken ankle makes running the marathon a genuinely extreme case, and 'even though' gives that surprising fact its strongest emphasis.
quests.nativeTip: A broken ankle days earlier makes finishing a marathon feel almost impossible.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: Some cultures eat with chopsticks, ___ others use forks and knives.
quests.completedSentence: Some cultures eat with chopsticks, whereas others use forks and knives.
quests.ruleExplanation: Both eating customs are simply being set beside each other as differing facts, with no surprise involved, which is exactly the plain comparison 'whereas' expresses.
quests.nativeTip: Neither habit is more surprising than the other — they're just being placed side by side.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: The north side of the building gets full sun all afternoon, ___ the south side stays shaded.
quests.completedSentence: The north side of the building gets full sun all afternoon, whereas the south side stays shaded.
quests.ruleExplanation: The two sides of the building are simply being contrasted as facts, and 'whereas' is the word for placing two differing situations side by side.
quests.nativeTip: Two facts about the building are just being laid out next to each other for comparison.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ the old software required a manual restart, the new version updates in the background.
quests.completedSentence: Whereas the old software required a manual restart, the new version updates in the background.
quests.ruleExplanation: The two software versions are being compared as differing facts rather than one surprising the other, which 'whereas' is built to express.
quests.nativeTip: Two versions of the software are simply being compared, not one overturning an expectation.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ my brother loves spicy food, I can't handle anything beyond mild.
quests.completedSentence: While my brother loves spicy food, I can't handle anything beyond mild.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two differing preferences are being set side by side rather than one going against an expectation, which is the comparison sense 'while' can carry.
quests.nativeTip: Two people's tastes are simply being placed against each other, not one defying expectation.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ the coastal towns rely on tourism, the inland regions depend mostly on farming.
quests.completedSentence: While the coastal towns rely on tourism, the inland regions depend mostly on farming.
quests.ruleExplanation: The two economies are being compared as parallel facts, and 'while' works here in that same comparative role as 'whereas'.
quests.nativeTip: Two regions' economies are simply being compared, with no surprise in either fact.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ some team members prefer working early mornings, others do their best work late at night.
quests.completedSentence: While some team members prefer working early mornings, others do their best work late at night.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two contrasting habits are being compared, not one undercutting an expectation, and 'while' fits that comparative role.
quests.nativeTip: Two working styles are simply being set against each other for comparison.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ the first draft focused on statistics, the revised version leads with a personal story.
quests.completedSentence: Whereas the first draft focused on statistics, the revised version leads with a personal story.
quests.ruleExplanation: This formal, document-review context calls for the more precise, editorial tone of 'whereas' over the more casual comparison word.
quests.nativeTip: This reads like an editorial note comparing two drafts, in a fairly formal tone.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: She listened to a podcast ___ she cleaned the kitchen.
quests.completedSentence: She listened to a podcast while she cleaned the kitchen.
quests.ruleExplanation: Both actions were simply overlapping in time rather than being compared as two different facts, so this is the simultaneous-time sense of 'while', not the comparison sense from earlier in this file.
quests.nativeTip: Both activities were happening in the same stretch of time, not being compared as two different situations.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ rent in the city center has doubled, salaries have barely moved.
quests.completedSentence: While rent in the city center has doubled, salaries have barely moved.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two separate trends are being compared here, not one action overlapping another in time, which is the comparison use of 'while' rather than its time-based one.
quests.nativeTip: Two economic trends are simply being placed side by side for comparison.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Contrast
quests.contextSentence: The concert tickets were pricey, ___ fans snapped them up within minutes.
quests.completedSentence: The concert tickets were pricey, but fans snapped them up within minutes.
quests.ruleExplanation: The high price makes the instant sellout surprising, and 'but' links these two full, independent clauses together in the middle of the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: High prices should have slowed sales down — did that actually happen?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the tickets were pricey, fans snapped them up within minutes.
quests.completedSentence: Although the tickets were pricey, fans snapped them up within minutes.
quests.ruleExplanation: Moving the contrasting idea to the front of the sentence needs a subordinating word, and 'although' can open a sentence this way, unlike the coordinating conjunction used for the same idea earlier.
quests.nativeTip: The same idea as before, but now the reason for surprise needs to open the sentence.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the reviews were mixed, ticket sales still broke records.
quests.completedSentence: Although the reviews were mixed, ticket sales still broke records.
quests.ruleExplanation: Starting a single sentence with the contrasting idea calls for a subordinating conjunction like 'although', since the coordinating option isn't built to open a sentence this way.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs to open with the surprising fact, which only one of these words can naturally do here.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ he already apologized twice, she still won't speak to him.
quests.completedSentence: Even though he already apologized twice, she still won't speak to him.
quests.ruleExplanation: The apologies are an established, completed fact, and 'even though' is used for a concession about something that has actually happened, not a possibility.
quests.nativeTip: The apologies already happened — this isn't a maybe, it's a done fact.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ he apologizes again, I doubt she'll change her mind.
quests.completedSentence: Even if he apologizes again, I doubt she'll change her mind.
quests.ruleExplanation: The apology here is only a future possibility, not a settled fact, so 'even if' is used for that hypothetical kind of concession.
quests.nativeTip: This apology hasn't happened yet — it's still just a possibility being imagined.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the report was reviewed twice, it still had errors.
quests.completedSentence: Even though the report was reviewed twice, it still had errors.
quests.ruleExplanation: The two reviews already happened, making this a concession about a real event, which 'even though' expresses rather than 'even if'.
quests.nativeTip: The double review already took place — this is a fact, not a hypothetical.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Contrast
quests.contextSentence: The proposal was risky, ___ the board approved it unanimously.
quests.completedSentence: The proposal was risky, yet the board approved it unanimously.
quests.ruleExplanation: A unanimous approval of something risky is unexpected, and 'yet' marks that surprising turn, much like 'but' would.
quests.nativeTip: A risky idea would usually meet resistance, not a unanimous yes.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ the pilot program ran over budget, the full rollout came in under cost.
quests.completedSentence: Whereas the pilot program ran over budget, the full rollout came in under cost.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pilot and the rollout are being compared as two differing outcomes, which is the comparison role 'whereas' plays, rather than a concession about one fact overturning an expectation.
quests.nativeTip: Two separate stages of the project are simply being compared to each other.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the numbers improve next year, the company plans to downsize regardless.
quests.completedSentence: Even if the numbers improve next year, the company plans to downsize regardless.
quests.ruleExplanation: The improvement is only a future possibility, and the downsizing plan stays fixed regardless, which is exactly the hypothetical, unaffected-outcome meaning of 'even if'.
quests.nativeTip: This future improvement is just a possibility, and the plan won't change either way.
